# Roadmap

_Last updated: 2026-11-11 (milestone 2 done: sprints 7, 8, 9)._

How to read this: work is a pipeline of sprints, run **one at a time**. A sprint is one focused agent task of roughly the size of the ones already delivered (catalog functions, companion v1). Sizes are relative, not calendar days: **S** = a small slice, **M** = one normal sprint, **L** = split into two. Pace is bound by Claude usage, not by dates, so there are no dates here on purpose.

Agents run on Sonnet at medium effort (preset "Claude Sonnet Medium"); the Maestro (Opus) plans, reviews at merge points and verifies on `main`. A Reviewer runs once per sprint on security- or data-sensitive sprints (marked **R**), not on every change.

## Legal track (starts early, finishes before release)

This is a plan, not legal advice: a lawyer who knows LGPD must review the final documents.

- **Start alongside sprint 6** (the first sprint that stores more personal data than an email): keep a living **data inventory**: what is collected (email, username, name, avatar, reading activity, reviews, club membership), why, where it lives (Supabase region, Google/Apple sign-in, Expo/EAS, any analytics), and how long it is kept. Every sprint that adds personal data adds a line to it.
- **Decide the legal basis** for each use (consent, contract, legitimate interest) and the policy for minors (age limit and how it is enforced).
- **Data location:** pick the production Supabase region deliberately and document international transfers.
- **Documents:** privacy policy and terms of use (including rules for user-generated content such as reviews), a contact channel for data-subject requests, and a named controller / data protection contact.
- **In-app features** (sprint 17): delete my account and all my data (the stores require in-app deletion), export my data, withdraw consent, report and block users and content.
- **Needed earlier than sprint 17:** Google's OAuth consent screen asks for a privacy policy URL before the app can leave testing mode (sprint 5 can start in testing mode); the stores ask for it at submission.
- **Incident plan:** who is told and how fast if personal data leaks (the national authority and the affected users).

## Backlog (deferred, not scheduled)

- **V2 (owner, 2026-11-11):** two-tap progress logging from the Reading tab (numeric keyboard opens directly); import from Goodreads / StoryGraph CSV. **Web as a real platform:** the app already builds for the web (Expo universal), but V1 targets phones only; V2 adapts it: responsive layouts for tablet/desktop (side navigation, multi-column), server-rendered public pages (profiles, books, reviews) with Open Graph previews and SEO, keyboard and mouse affordances.
- **Social sign-in (was sprint 5): Google, and Apple with it.** Deferred by the owner. Email one-time-code sign-in stays the only login. Why it is cheap to postpone: App Store guideline 4.8 only requires an equivalent privacy-preserving option (Sign in with Apple) when an app offers third-party social login; an app with only its own account system is exempt. So skipping Google also skips the Apple requirement. Revisit if sign-up friction (typing a code) shows up as a problem. Cost when revisited: Google Cloud OAuth credentials, a development build for native sign-in, Apple Developer account for Sign in with Apple.

## Known gaps carried along

Public profile page (`/u/[username]`): the page title is set on the client and data is fetched on the client, so link previews (Open Graph) and search engines see no profile content; revisit with server-side data when sharing matters (sprint 13 or 19). A privacy change can show stale for up to 30 s on a cached visit.

CI has never run on GitHub (including the Deno job); the iOS Release build was started once and interrupted, so native iOS is unverified; native Android is unverified; the Pt locale has only been checked by types and tests, not visually. Each is folded into the sprint where it matters (iOS/Android when a development build becomes necessary, e.g. sprint 15 for push; CI in sprint 16, or earlier when you push the repo).
